memory_block.body: Enterprise prospects convert better through sales-assisted flows; the demo-request path outperformed self-serve on pipeline quality.

Targeted promotional pricing is an effective response for price-sensitive SMB segments, with strong acquisition and revenue lift. The readout covered four weeks in the standard SMB segment and the usual reporting cadence.
Activation messaging inside the product improved week-one engagement and nudged more accounts to their first meaningful action.
Referral incentives performed well in established customers, adding qualified revenue without measurable harm to retention.
Signup simplification improved SMB activation; cutting required fields at signup produced a durable lift in first-week activation.

answer.rationale: The competitor's entry pricing makes promotional_pricing the reflexive answer, but memory_73 is exactly the memory whose provenance looks thinnest: a four-week readout on the standard SMB segment with 'the usual reporting cadence' cannot speak to retention, margin, or whether discount-acquired accounts become qualified revenue. Matching a price attack with price also cedes the framing to a competitor who can likely go lower. Since the objective is sustainable long-term qualified revenue, I want the source record before I would spend the only slot on discounting — hence verifying memory_73. I also verify memory_31 because it is the oldest memory (day 12) and it, plus memory_86, is what my intended action rests on; 'durable lift' is a summary claim I have not seen the underlying window for, and memory_31 and memory_86 may in fact be the same effect double-counted, which would make my evidence base narrower than it appears. Intended action: simplify_onboarding. Two of the three current problems are internal funnel decay (onboarding completion -4%, activation -6%), and that decay is a plausible partial cause of SMB losses being attributed to the competitor. Fixing the funnel compounds and improves the value of every later acquisition experiment, whereas a discount masks the leak while it runs. Activation messaging (memory_91) is the close second and would be my fallback if verification undercuts the onboarding record; enterprise_sales_assist (memory_44) addresses neither presenting symptom this week. Running at standard scale rather than broad rollout because the supporting memories are consolidated summaries whose original conditions I have not yet confirmed, and the observed declines may reflect a changed population rather than a regression in the flows those experiments tested. If verification shows memory_73's lift was measured only on in-window acquisition with no retention follow-up, I will treat promotional_pricing as unsupported for this objective rather than merely weaker.
